steps.title: Check foreign keys
steps.text: reported_by and zone_id must point to existing rows, so user 2 and zone 1 are looked up through their primary keys.

steps.title: Fill defaults
steps.text: status becomes reported and observed_at becomes NOW(). verified_at, verified_by and resolved_at stay NULL.

steps.title: Write the row
steps.text: A new row is stored with a generated incident_id.

steps.title: Alert trigger fires
steps.text: The AFTER INSERT trigger picks a radius from severity: medium means 2000 m. Users within that radius are collected, and the reporter (user 2) is always excluded. Only user 3 is close enough, at about 1.06 km.

steps.title: Write the alert
steps.text: One incident_alert row is inserted for user 3, and pg_notify publishes the recipient count on the incident_alerts channel.

title: Create: record a sighting and refresh the animal

steps.title: Check foreign keys
steps.text: animal 1, user 1 and zone 1 must exist before the sighting is accepted.

steps.title: Insert inside the CTE
steps.text: The sighting row is written first. observed_at defaults to NOW() and RETURNING hands the new row to the outer statement.

steps.title: Match the animal
steps.text: The returned row is joined to animal through animal_id, so exactly one animal row is targeted.

steps.title: Update the animal
steps.text: last_known_location, last_location_updated_at and last_sighting_id are copied from the new sighting. Both writes share one statement, so they commit or fail together.

steps.title: Read the officer
steps.text: Authority 3 is found by primary key.

steps.title: Availability guard
steps.text: Officer C is available, so the row survives. For an unavailable officer the SELECT returns nothing and no assignment is created, without raising an error.

steps.title: Check foreign keys
steps.text: Incident 4 and authority 3 both exist.

steps.title: Write the row
steps.text: The assignment starts with status assigned and assigned_at set to NOW().

title: Read: officers with their zones
sql: JOIN zones z ON z.zone_id = a.assigned_zone_id

steps.title: Scan authority
steps.text: Every authority row is read, the left side of the join.

steps.title: Join on zone
steps.text: For each row, the zone whose zone_id equals assigned_zone_id is looked up.

steps.title: Project and sort
steps.text: Only the selected columns are returned, ordered by zone name and then officer name.

steps.title: Locate the row
steps.text: The primary key index finds incident 4 directly.

steps.title: Guard on status
steps.text: The extra status check keeps the update idempotent: incident 4 is still reported so it passes, and running the statement again would touch zero rows.

steps.title: Write the new version
steps.text: PostgreSQL stores a new row version with status, verified_at and verified_by changed. Other columns and rows are untouched.

title: Update: officer goes off duty with history

steps.title: Update the officer
steps.text: available changes from true to false for authority 1.

steps.title: Return the new state
steps.text: RETURNING exposes the updated row to the outer INSERT, so the snapshot always matches what was just written.

steps.title: Append the snapshot
steps.text: A history row records the officer, zone, location and availability. The schema has no history trigger, so doing it in one statement keeps both tables consistent.

steps.title: Mark the parent
steps.text: Incident 1 is located and marked for removal.

steps.title: Cascade to conflicts
steps.text: ON DELETE CASCADE removes human_wildlife_conflict rows that reference incident 1.

steps.title: Cascade to assignments
steps.text: response_assignment rows for the incident are removed next.

steps.title: Cascade to actions
steps.text: Actions belonging to the removed assignment go with it.

steps.title: Cascade to alerts
steps.text: incident_alert also cascades from incident, so the alert sent for this incident is removed. The deletion is complete.

steps.title: Locate the row
steps.text: Authority 1 is found by primary key.

steps.title: Check references
steps.text: response_assignment.assigned_to and response_action.performed_by both use ON DELETE RESTRICT, and rows in each still point to authority 1.

steps.title: Statement fails
steps.text: PostgreSQL raises a foreign key violation and cancels the statement. Every table stays exactly as it was, even though incident.verified_by would have used SET NULL.
